post.caption: Hackmanite changes color in sunlight. It is a variety of sodalite, a stone named for its sodium. Sodalite looks like lapis lazuli but lacks its gold flecks of pyrite. In 1906, 130 tons of Ontario sodalite went to England. Freshly dug in Greenland or Quebec, it is pale to deep violet. In sunlight it fades to gray or greenish white. Days in the dark bring the violet back, a trait called tenebrescence. The change can repeat practically forever, until heat ends it for good. Hackmanite honors Finnish geologist Victor Hackman. In 2022, researchers in Finland traced the change to shifting sodium atoms.
